headline: Around 100 employees laid off by Daraz in Bangladesh
summary: The Alibaba-owned e-commerce giant reportedly cut jobs as part of a cost-saving effort, marking another round of workforce reductions in the country.
details: Daraz Bangladesh has reportedly laid off around 100 employees on May 6 and 7, according to several former employees who were affected by the cuts.
Former managerial-level staff said the dismissals were communicated in brief meetings and were part of a wider cost-saving effort by the Alibaba-owned company.
Affected employees claimed that the layoffs were sudden and that the company cited cost-cutting measures and operational optimisation as the reasons.
Some former staff members noted that Daraz Bangladesh has operated at a loss since its inception, unlike its operations in Pakistan and Sri Lanka.
It was also alleged that Alibaba will not make any new unconditional investments in Daraz Bangladesh until the company can demonstrate profitability.
In a statement, Daraz denied the claims of exiting the market, stating they remain firmly committed to Bangladesh and continue to operate normally.
The company added that it regularly reviews its organisational structure and resource allocation to align with evolving business priorities.
This follows previous rounds of layoffs in February 2024, which reportedly affected about 35 percent of the workforce, and dozens of employees in February 2023.
The job cuts are part of a broader restructuring of Daraz's South Asian operations, including similar reductions in Nepal.
caption:

Daraz Bangladesh has reportedly laid off around 100 employees on May 6 and 7, according to several former employees who were affected by the cuts.

Affected employees claimed that the layoffs were sudden and that the company cited cost-cutting measures and operational optimisation as the reasons.

Some former staff members noted that Daraz Bangladesh has operated at a loss since its inception, unlike its operations in Pakistan and Sri Lanka.

It was also alleged that Alibaba will not make any new unconditional investments in Daraz Bangladesh until the company can demonstrate profitability.

In a statement, Daraz denied the claims of exiting the market, stating they remain firmly committed to Bangladesh and continue to operate normally.

The company added that it regularly reviews its organisational structure and resource allocation to align with evolving business priorities.

This follows previous rounds of layoffs in February 2024, which reportedly affected about 35 percent of the workforce, and dozens of employees in February 2023.

The job cuts are part of a broader restructuring of Daraz's South Asian operations, including similar reductions in Nepal.

headline_marked: Two youths from Jamalpur [[killed in drone strike]] while fighting for Russia
headline: Two youths from Jamalpur killed in drone strike while fighting for Russia
summary: Maful and Arif, who had been missing for 17 days, were reportedly killed in the Russia-Ukraine conflict.
details: Two young men from Madarganj Upazila in Jamalpur have been killed in a drone strike while fighting for the Russian army against Ukraine.
The deceased are identified as Maful, alias Mofiz, 23, from Karaichara Union, and Arif Hossain, 27, from Sidhuli Union.
The two had been missing for 17 days before their relatives learned of their deaths through an audio message circulated on social media on Monday morning.
Madarganj Upazila administrator (UNO) Sumon Choudhury stated that the duo had traveled abroad via a local broker group rather than through official channels.
The UNO has promised to inform higher authorities and take action if the families submit a written application regarding the matter.
caption:

The two had been missing for 17 days before their relatives learned of their deaths through an audio message circulated on social media on Monday morning.

Madarganj Upazila administrator (UNO) Sumon Choudhury stated that the duo had traveled abroad via a local broker group rather than through official channels.

The UNO has promised to inform higher authorities and take action if the families submit a written application regarding the matter.
